Looking at the historical data, the highest yields come from combinations using **6-iodoquinoline** as electrophile and **5-methyl-1-(oxan-2-yl)-4-(4,4,5,5-tetramethyl-1,3,2-dioxaborolan-2-yl)indazole** or **[5-methyl-1-(oxan-2-yl)indazol-4-yl]boronic acid** as nucleophile, with **tricyclohexylphosphane** ligand and either **cesium fluoride** or **lithium 2-methylpropan-2-olate** base. The best yield (89.03) used lithium 2-methylpropan-2-olate in DMF, while another high yield (88.99) used cesium fluoride in acetonitrile. To explore promising sparse combinations, I'll focus on the ligand and base fields that have shown high performance.

Looking at the historical data, the highest yields (96.97% and 96.19%) were achieved with **bis(1-adamantyl)-butylphosphane** as ligand and **lithium 2-methylpropan-2-olate** as base, using either 6-iodoquinoline or 6-bromoquinoline with the pinacol boronic ester nucleophile. The combination of this bulky, electron-rich ligand with a strong base appears to promote efficient transmetalation while suppressing protodeboronation. I will suggest focusing on this promising ligand-base pair.
